title: Open air X-ray diffractometer for crystallography and structural phase transitions
author: Alam

steps.title: Insulate XRD electronics and wiring
steps.instruction: Wrap all XRD electronics and electrical wires that will be exposed to temperature extremes with thermal insulation material; ensure the insulation also shields the components from water‑vapor condensation.

steps.title: Install water‑condensation protection
steps.instruction: Place water‑resistant containers beneath the sample area to collect any droplets formed from condensation; line exposed parts with water‑resistant material, leaving only the sample holder open for the specimen.

steps.title: Assemble liquid‑nitrogen cooling unit
steps.instruction: Set up a liquid‑nitrogen (LN₂) container on a stable, insulating base; partially cover the container with an insulated layer that can be adjusted; attach a long flexible exhaust pipe to the container, bend the pipe so its outlet directs cold vapor onto the sample surface.

steps.title: Adjust insulation for desired cooling
steps.instruction: For higher cooling, open the LN₂ container (remove or loosen the insulated cover) so room air warms the LN₂ and increases vapor flow; for lower cooling, fully cover the container to reduce vapor release.

steps.title: Mount CrN thin‑film sample
steps.instruction: Place the epitaxial CrN thin film on the XRD sample holder, ensuring the orientation [100]CrN‖[100]MgO, [110]CrN‖[110]MgO, [001]CrN‖[001]MgO on the MgO(001) substrate; keep the holder open so the nitrogen vapor can reach the film.

steps.title: Configure XRD measurement parameters
steps.instruction: Program the diffractometer to scan the 002 reflections of both MgO and CrN (within ~2° of each other) in repeated mode; set the 2θ range to include MgO 002 (kβ 38.59°, kα1 42.90°, kα2 44.??°) and CrN 002 (kβ 39.19°, kα1 43.54°, kα2 44.??°) as well as the 004 peaks (MgO 004 kα1 94.11°, kα2 94.40°; CrN 004 kα1 95.92°). Note that the X‑ray beam contains three wavelengths: kβ = 1.3923 Å, kα1 = 1.54059 Å, kα2 = 1.54439 Å. Use four‑significant‑figure angle acquisition.

steps.title: Determine sample temperature from MgO peak
steps.instruction: Measure the MgO 002 peak position at each scan, calculate the lattice constant a₀ = 4.213 Å, compute the change Δa, and obtain temperature using T(K) = 293 K + Δa / (a₀ α_MgO) with α_MgO = 9.84 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹.

steps.title: Cool sample from 293 K to 203 K
steps.instruction: Fill the LN₂ container, open the exhaust pipe, and adjust the insulation to achieve a gradual temperature drop; continuously record XRD spectra of the 002 peaks while the temperature decreases to 203 K.

steps.title: Warm sample and record spectra
steps.instruction: Increase insulation coverage to reduce vapor flow, allowing the sample to warm back toward 293 K; continue recording XRD spectra throughout the warming cycle.

steps.title: Analyze lattice‑constant versus temperature
steps.instruction: Extract the CrN out‑of‑plane lattice constant a⊥ from the 002 peak (initially 4.152 Å at 293 K); plot a⊥ versus temperature; fit the data to a⊥(T)=4.152 Å − 0.008 Å / [1 + exp((T − T_N)/ΔT)] to obtain the transition temperature T_N ≈ 256 ± 6 K. If a linear fit is forced, calculate α_CrN = 2.9 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. Verify the epitaxial lattice mismatch (a_CrN − a_MgO)/a_MgO × 100 ≈ 1.45 %.

steps.title: Optional temperature sensing for other samples
steps.instruction: For non‑epitaxial specimens, either use a reference material with known thermal expansion to infer temperature or install a temperature sensor on the sample holder for direct measurement.
